headSHASemantics: This is the exact hosted-validation test implementation commit. The following documentation-only evidence commit does not change renderer production or test code.
scope: Hosted evidence for the Phase 6 native JSON Canvas surface and the static Excalidraw package through the existing restrictive Phase 5 WebKit session. The slice adds no production behavior or policy.

success: JSON Canvas decodes a deterministic two-node document, mounts in a real AppKit window through NSHostingController, and yields a nonempty rendered PNG.

The Excalidraw package validates into a temporary staging root, mounts through the real restrictive WikiAppWebViewSession, receives its bridge-authorized input, renders svg.scene, and responds to bounded keyboard zoom and pan.
The hosted Excalidraw test replaces the SwiftUI root and observes the existing session close lifecycle.
error: No failure-path behavior is changed. Existing package validation, bridge authorization, session failure, safe-mode, and Source-fallback tests remain the governing error evidence.
boundary: The Excalidraw test uses the production renderer-package scheme URL, validated package resource provider, version-pinned reservation, authorized-input reader, and content-world broker. It does not use the permissive HTTP and WebSocket positive-control harness.
The test sends no external activation, performs no file resolution, and makes no HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket, or arbitrary URL request.
The native test uses only local decoded data and a local AppKit window. It has no host action handler or file/network operation.
coverage.cancellation: Every asynchronous hosted wait polls with Task.sleep, checks cancellation, and has a 15-second timeout. The suite is serialized behind HostedAppKitTestGate.
coverage.teardown: Both tests release the AppKit gate, remove their windows, close the hosted WebKit session, and remove the temporary Excalidraw validator root.

bidirectionalResolution.command: inventory=plans/dynamic-renderers-phase6-hosted-validation-test-inventory.json && jq -e '(.productionPaths | length > 0) and (.testPaths | length > 0) and all(.productionPaths[]; ((.path | type == "string" and length > 0) and (.symbols | type == "array" and length > 0) and (.tests | type == "array" and length > 0))) and all(.testPaths[]; type == "string" and length > 0)' "$inventory" >/dev/null && while IFS= read -r listedPath; do test -f "$listedPath" || { echo "inventory production path is missing: $listedPath" >&2; exit 1; }; done < <(jq -r '.productionPaths[].path' "$inventory") && while IFS= read -r listedPath; do test -f "$listedPath" || { echo "inventory test path is missing: $listedPath" >&2; exit 1; }; done < <(jq -r '.testPaths[]' "$inventory") && while IFS= read -r testName; do functionName=${testName##*.}; matches=$(rg -l -F "func ${functionName}(" $(jq -r '.testPaths[]' "$inventory") | wc -l | tr -d ' '); test "$matches" -eq 1 || { echo "inventory test did not resolve exactly once: $testName" >&2; exit 1; }; done < <(jq -r '[.productionPaths[].tests[]] | unique[]' "$inventory")

excluded: Phase 5 production security policy, navigation, bridge, CSP, trusted activation, safe mode, and Source-fallback behavior
JSON Canvas typed-link and host-action semantics
external URL activation, network traffic, package management, Phase 7 work, and PR state
honestCoverageLimits: The JSON Canvas hosted assertion records a nonempty bitmap and deterministic document outline. It is not a pixel-baseline golden image and does not toggle system appearance, Reduce Motion, AppKit focus routing, or VoiceOver output.

The Excalidraw hosted interaction proves bridge-backed rendering plus synthetic keyboard pan and zoom only. It does not exercise pointer or wheel delivery, every supported element, or an external-link redemption.

The optional Phase 5 HTTP and WebSocket positive-control test is environment-bound because it requires a trusted loopback identity. It was observed separately when that local identity was provisioned; this evidence suite neither depends on nor relaxes that requirement.
The hosted package test is local-only and exercises no network path. It cannot establish behavior for a browser process or entitlement configuration different from this macOS SwiftPM environment.
